methods.label: Combine conjugation with a sign change
methods.explanation:
Conjugation changes \(i\) to \(-i\), while replacing a variable by its negative changes the signs of its odd powers. These two operations fit the alternating coefficient pattern.

Let \(P(t)\) denote the displayed polynomial, and let \(\overline z=a-bi\) be the conjugate of \(z=a+bi\). Conjugation preserves sums and products. Because every \(c_j\) is real,
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(-\overline z)
&=c_4\overline z^{\,4}-ic_3\overline z^{\,3}\\
&\quad+c_2\overline z^{\,2}-ic_1\overline z+c_0\\
&=\overline{P(z)}=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore \(-\overline z\) must also be a solution. Since
\[
-\overline z=-(a-bi)=-a+bi,
\]
the answer is \(\boxed{-a+bi}\), choice C. The identity remains valid when coefficients vanish; if \(a=0\), the guaranteed root simply coincides with the original root.
